said:
A small colony with real dependencies
Port Vesper can prepare food, purify water and repair much of its equipment. Specialist electronics, medicines and parts for the Peregrine come from elsewhere.
Resupply is slow. Stocks and delivery times must therefore be established in advance. A shortage arises through consumption, delay or damage, not because the Chronicler needs tension at that moment.
Food and everyday supplies
Residents mainly eat cultivated proteins, grain products from imported stocks and locally grown vegetables. Nacre has native life, but it is not automatically edible for humans. Edible coastal crops come from controlled beds containing imported Earth species.
| Product | Origin | Seller or distribution point |
| Hot meals | Prepared from locally grown vegetables and proteins, supplemented with imported grain, oil and herbs. | Sana in Commons, at mealtimes. A simple meal normally costs 4 credits. |
| Field rations | Shelf-stable portions, assembled locally from controlled stocks. | Sana in Commons; normally 6 credits per day's supply. |
| Drinking water | Purified seawater, stored in the settlement. | Ordinary quantities are free at taps in Commons and Guest Quarters. |
| Hot drink | Cultivated herbal tea or imported coffee. | Sana in Commons; ordinary herbal drink 50 bits, coffee more expensive and sometimes unavailable. |
| Filters, seals and cable materials | Repaired or assembled from local work stock; some raw materials are imported. | Tessa at the Workshop counter. |
| Field lamps, batteries and measuring equipment | Mostly imported and locally maintained. | Request through Mara; Tessa checks and issues them in Workshop. Purchase or registered loan. |
| Dressings and medical supplies | Sterile supplies and medicines are largely imported. | Edda in Medical Bay, after assessing their intended use. |

There is no general shop selling everything without limit. Mara manages orders and contract supplies; Sana, Tessa and Edda manage their own distribution.
What is produced here
Small-scale cultivation and water purification are settlement installations. They do not need additional accessible locations at the start.
| Product or service | Who | Where | Resources required |
| Vegetables and cultivated protein | Support team; Sana plans consumption. | Enclosed growing modules near Guest Quarters. | Water, nutrients, seeds or cultures, energy and maintenance. |
| Meals and rations | Sana, with residents on kitchen duty. | Commons kitchen. | Food stocks, drinking water, energy and packaging. |
| Drinking water | Support team; Tessa has technical responsibility. | Purification installation near Workshop. | Seawater, energy, filters and membrane parts. |
| Repaired devices | Tessa and the field mechanic. | Workshop. | Damaged device, suitable parts, tools and labour. |
| Cables and simple connectors | Technical team. | Electronics workbench in Workshop. | Insulated wire, connector housings, contacts and protective sheathing. |
| Non-critical brackets and housings | Technical team. | Small fabrication bench in Workshop. | Suitable metal or polymer, energy and a checked design. |

The fabrication bench cannot make every object. Being able to produce a shape does not mean the material is suitable for a pressure airlock, medical implant or experimental drive.
What is gathered outside
Along the Coastal Service Path are a few managed coastal beds with salt-tolerant Earth crops. A short marked access from the path is sufficient; no eleventh location is added.
Under certain conditions, the player may:
Harvest coastal vegetables, with permission and within the harvest limit.
Salvage washed-up human materials, such as detached cable protection or a damaged transport container.
Sample rock and native organisms for research.
Samples are not food. Salvaged material is identified and checked first. A recognisable serial number may show that an item still belongs to someone else.
Bad weather may make harvesting or salvage impossible. A depleted spot does not refill every time someone looks at it again.
The first learnable craft Field Electronics
The stranger can learn from Tessa Rook to maintain and repair simple field equipment.
The workplace is the Electronics Bench in Workshop: an antistatic workbench with measuring instruments, hand tools and a protected test power supply.
| Stage | What you learn | Example |
| Beginner | Recognise damage, clean contacts and check simple connections. | Examine an unreliable field lamp. |
| Trained | Repair cables and standard connectors. | Make a damaged measurement cable usable again. |
| Expert | Locate faults in linked systems and choose suitable replacement parts. | Isolate the fault in the relay cabinet at Ridge Shelter. |
| Master | Design, test and document a difficult repair. | Deliver a reliable emergency solution for expedition equipment. |

A high craft rank grants no automatic authorisation to work on life support or the drive. Those require separate training, permission and checks.
First lesson and first assignment
Tessa offers a supervised three-hour lesson for 15 credits, including practice materials. She may also offer it as a favour in return for a useful job.
The first assignment is a field lamp with a broken cable. Tessa has the player examine it first, then repair it and finally test it. The lamp belongs to the workshop; a successful repair does not automatically mean it is given to you.
The player can then repair a measurement cable Niko needs for the investigation at Orison Ridge. This connects the craft directly to people and the main assignment.
Failure and moving forward
A failed repair has a concrete outcome: extra material consumption, a fault that remains or a damaged part. A test may reveal that error before the device is used.
Practice equipment runs at a safe test voltage. Dangerous procedures do not become available merely because the player might get a favourable roll.
A successful repair provides practice. Repeatedly repairing the same simple fault eventually ceases to advance professional skill.
Stocks payment and scarcity
The settlement distinguishes between:
Available trade stock: available for sale.
Work stock: issued for a registered job.
Emergency reserve: releasable only by the responsible person.
Expedition stock: allocated to the Peregrine.
Transfers between these stocks change actual quantities. They do not create new parts.
An assignment specifies in advance who pays and from which budget. If the player uses allocated research materials, they do not have to buy them personally first. Crafted or repaired work can be sold if there is genuine demand.
For the Chronicler
Let the economy primarily create choices: repair or replace, wait for delivery or seek an alternative, borrow something or ask a favour. Avoid turning the first research phase into constantly buying food and settling small bills.
The most important economic conflict remains visible: what can the Peregrine take without leaving Port Vesper vulnerable? This affects supplies, trust and responsibility at the same time.
